sourceIndependence.diagramRole: Shared event-name order can support a proposed cross-context match; identical diagrams do not prove identical melodies.
sourceIndependence.independentMeaning: The candidate landmark is specified by the source structure before looking for a favorable pitch residual. This is different from independent performer, tradition or historical witness.

existingAudioEvidenceLimits: The endpoint artifact explicitly states no syllable alignment and permits octave error. Its last periodic window is not yet independently verified as the same Etnachta syllable/state in both recordings.
Four RMS groups were imposed from the sheet. Haftarah grouping changes at the higher threshold; group index alone cannot certify row4 correspondence.
Whole-phrase duration and different MP3 bytes are not terminal-accent melody measurements.
No new listening/transcription or f0 estimate was performed in this audit.

conditionalPitchTest.model: For correctly corresponding positive-frequency anchors, Haftarah y_i = k * Torah x_i with one k>0
conditionalPitchTest.oneAnchor: Given x1,y1>0, k=y1/x1 fits exactly; one pair cannot reject unrestricted uniform transposition.
conditionalPitchTest.interpretation: A residual supported away from zero after alignment, octave and estimation-uncertainty checks excludes one uniform factor at these landmarks only. Zero residual leaves the rest of both melodies untested.
conditionalPitchTest.landmarkType: An accent may carry a motif or contour. Do not assume one accent equals one stationary note. The chosen comparable subevent or contour statistic must be declared before inspecting f0 results.

steps: Verify the spoken/sung accent-name sequence and actual row boundaries separately in each recording; annotate the Tipcha and Etnachta intervals without displaying pitch estimates.

If corresponding syllables can be identified, freeze a comparable vocal subevent or contour measurement and all exclusions before inspecting f0. Preserve uncertainty rather than moving the window to make the residual small or large.

Check octave assignment, voiced/unvoiced transitions and within-window pitch variation. Use an estimator and uncertainty assessment appropriate to the actual recording, not rounded endpoint values as exact frequencies.
Evaluate both candidate anchors and their residual under the declared rule. This extends already exposed data and is not automatically a blind prediction.
If alignment remains ambiguous, return the possible intervals or obtain a source-qualified timed/staff transcription; do not convert row labels into assumed timestamps.
